newsitem.title: UK: Euro shares up as U.S. Fed mesmerises markets.
newsitem.headline: Euro shares up as U.S. Fed mesmerises markets.

text.p: European stock markets mostly rose on Tuesday, but investors sat firmly on the fence before a U.S. Federal Reserve meeting discussing the issue which has haunted this year's bull runs -- interest rates.
The dollar was quietly mixed but again dealers were mesmerised by a two-day meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) starting on Tuesday.
With the United States apparently enjoying low-inflation economic growth, logic dictates that the FOMC -- the Fed's policy-making arm -- should leave rates unchanged.
But markets face a long wait to hear whether logic will prevail as no announcement on interest rates is expected until the meeting ends late on Wednesday.
Tuesday was the third anniversary of a U.S. interest rate hike which caught investors off guard and sent share prices tumbling globally.
This time nobody is taking any chances.

"The risk now is clearly that they'll do something as the market doesn't expect anything," said Philippe Brossard, head of research at ABN Amro in Paris. "The (U.S.) economy is strong but inflation is not. It seems as if the good news on inflation is the main focus."
In London, investors had the additional worry of a regular meeting of British monetary authorities on Wednesday.

"Recent figures show there's really no threat of inflation heating up, so there's no reason to raise rates," said one London share dealer. "But I would have thought the market needs to get these meetings out of the way."
By noon the main European bourses except Paris were up despite a small FOMC-inspired drop on Wall Street overnight.
London's FTSE-100 index was up 16.6 points at 4,274.4 while Frankfurt's DAX, which closed at a record on Monday, rose a further 7.83 to 3,070.12.
But Paris slipped back from modest early gains as FOMC jitters set in, with the CAC-40 down 4.2 points at 2,504.35.

Everywhere caution was the watchword, reflected in the Dow Jones industrial average which closed down 6.93 points at 6,806.16 on Monday. That included the foreign exchange markets, where the dollar flirted with 1.64 marks in quiet trade.

"With the FOMC meeting, I don't think anyone's going to want to do very much, so I think we're in for a fairly range-bound day until we get something out of the FOMC," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank.
The dollar was at 1.6401 marks and 122.10 yen at midmorning, down from its late Monday European level of 1.6436 marks but up from 121.83 yen.
The dollar may no longer be hitting highs but the tone remains firm before a meeting this weekend of finance ministers of the Group of Seven (G7) industrial nations in Berlin.

"The strength of the dollar is being underpinned by comments by Japanese officials playing down prospects of concerted intervention coming out of the G7 meeting," said Adam Chester, international bond strategist at Yamaichi International.
"It's not doing very much against the mark so, it's rather yen weakness against the dollar now."

U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin repeated overnight that a strong dollar was in the United States' interest, and Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said the dollar was unlikely to be lowered through international cooperation.

Gold also showed some unaccustomed strength with dealers saying it had been oversold in its recent slide. Bullion was fixed at $346.30, $2 up from the previous morning fix but little changed from a $346.25 London close on Monday.
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT
The dollar was at 1.6401 marks and 122.10 yen after closing in Europe at 1.6436 marks and 121.83 yen on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1130 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was 16.6 points higher at 4,274.4.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was 7.83 points higher at 3,070.12.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 4.20 at 2,504.35.
PRECIOUS METALS - Gold was fixed at $346.30 an ounce after closing in Europe on Monday at $346.25. Silver was unchanged at $4.91.
